DEV↔Core account-linking workstream (started 2026-08-06, from Erin's broken "relink MyMLH" test).

**How the system works (verified against both codebases + prod DBs):**
- Core creates unclaimed "shadow" users for DEV accounts (owns Customer.io/email). The ONLY auto-merge is `UserIdentifier#claim!` at first MyMLH sign-in with a byte-identical email — OAuth-linking from DEV settings never merges.
- ~3.45M DEV `mlh` identities; 99.98% are uid-only (Core-seeded via DEV admin API, no `auth_data_dump`) → everyone saw "No email found. Please relink" with the Connect button hidden. Only ~700 real OAuth links ever.
- Core: ~4.77M users, 8.7% claimed; DEV-linked users 98% unclaimed. Zero same-email claimed/shadow twins (creation-time dedup works). `user_merges` audit: ~45/mo.
- Support answer for merging: "sign in to MyMLH with your DEV email" — that claims + absorbs the shadow.

**PRs:** forem https://github.com/forem/forem/pull/23699 (merged) · core https://github.com/MLH-Engineering/core/pull/2975 (merged) · forem follow-up https://github.com/forem/forem/pull/23702 — repoints uid-only (admin-seeded) identities on re-auth + touches profile_updated_at so core's shadow merge gets its `mlh_user_id` signal. Gap found via Erin's repro 2026-08-07: differing-uid guard made Reconnect a silent no-op for the dominant case. Her test pair: shadow 019fd7c8-355f…, MLH user 019fd7c7-906b… — should merge once she re-auths after #23702 deploys.

**Approved decisions (Jon):**
- Use "MLH" not "MyMLH" in user-facing copy.
- Core PR (`dev-sync-email-trust` branch): (1) gate email trust on DEV `confirmed_at` in `user_sync.rb` — no primary identifier / no email-based resolve until confirmed (closes pre-hijack vectors; ~140k unconfirmed DEV registrants); (2) merge pure shadows via `UserMergingService` in `upsert_dev_profile` instead of silent re-point (was orphan-hard-deleting consent data).
- Forem PR (`mlh-identity-settings-cta` branch): sign-in-to-MLH CTA replacing the dead-end error, working relink (Authenticator refreshes payload on existing identity), en/fr/pt locales.
- Shadow creation timing stays at DEV signup (needed for CIO person, dev:<id> stitch, create-time-only consent signals). DEV's confirmation email is sent by DEV via CIO transactional keyed by email — no Core dependency.

Related: [[customerio-email-migration]]. Unrelated: uncommitted `Moderator::MergeUser` dedup changes in the forem working tree — Jon didn't recognize them; left untouched.

name: customerio-cli-access
description: "The `cio` CLI reaches Customer.io Design Studio, layouts and snippets far more cheaply than browser automation — plus its one blocking bug"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 5b6eaee2-ac02-4908-babd-8881c6a6886f
  modified: 2026-08-17T14:24:58.601Z
---

`cio` (`@customerio/cli`, npm global) is installed and authenticated against
MLH's workspace. It is the right tool for Customer.io work — vastly cheaper and
safer than driving `fly.customer.io` with browser automation.

- Workspace/environment id for the DEV+MLH shared workspace: **152482**.
- `cio schema` (works offline) lists every resource; `cio api <path> --params
  '{"environment_id":"152482"}'` calls it. Use `--read-only` for exploration
  and `--dry-run` to validate writes.
- Covers what the UI covers: `design_studio/{components,emails,folders,global_styles}`,
  `snippets`, `layouts` — including `GET /layouts/{id}/transactional_messages`,
  which is authoritative when the layout page's usage counter is not.
- `PATCH design_studio/global_styles` takes `{create:[...], update:{...}}`, so
  new tokens can be added without touching existing ones. Variable tokens
  (color/radius/spacing/font) take `type`+`value`; component tokens
  (button/link/section/divider/textStyle) take `properties`.

**Blocking bug:** `--json` rejects any `\n` inside a JSON string value
("contains control character"), inline *and* via `@file`. Author Design Studio
component/email content as a **single line** — that is how the platform stores
it anyway. Raw `curl` is not an escape hatch: the `sa_live_` token is not a
bearer token, it must be exchanged for a short-lived JWT.

**`--dry-run` never reaches the server** — it only checks JSON locally, so a wrong body
shape passes and then 400s for real. When `cio schema` shows `request_body_schema: null`,
read the body from the cached spec `~/.cio/cache/specs/openapi.json` (`components.schemas`)
instead of guessing. Example: snippet PUT is `{"snippet": {"name", "value"}}`, both required.

**Permission gate:** in auto mode, Claude Code's classifier blocks *mutating*
`cio api` calls (`-X POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE`) as external writes. Reads,
`--read-only` and `--dry-run` pass. Stage the whole build as a script, then
either have Jon run it with `! python3 <script>` or add a Bash permission rule.
Plan for this up front — discovering it mid-build wastes a pass.

See [[customerio-email-migration]].

def set_perform_deliveries
    self.perform_deliveries = ForemInstance.smtp_enabled?
  end

  def set_delivery_options
    # A mailer action may decline to send by returning before mail() -- Rails
    # then swaps in a NullMail. Every branch below touches mail(), which with
    # @_mail_was_called still false would render the message the action
    # deliberately skipped, and blow up on its unset ivars.
    return unless @_mail_was_called

    if deliver_via_customerio?
      # Deliverable on a Customer.io-only instance (no SMTP creds) must still
      # send, so the per-message flag overrides the SMTP-based default above.
      message.perform_deliveries = true
      options = @customerio_delivery_options || {}
      options = options.merge(
        # identifiers are always controller-resolved and intentionally override
        # anything passed via customerio_delivery_options.
        identifiers: customerio_identifiers,
        # layout data is a floor, not a ceiling: a mailer may override any of
        # it by passing the same key through customerio_delivery_options.
        message_data: layout_message_data.merge(options[:message_data] || {}),
      )

      # Both methods receive the same options; each reads the keys it needs.
      # customerio_event_name reaching the transactional path is harmless --
      # Customerio::SendEmailRequest drops fields the App API does not define.
      method = deliver_via_customerio_event? ? DeliveryMethods::CustomerIoEvent : DeliveryMethods::CustomerIo
      message.delivery_method(method, options)
    else
      mail.delivery_method.settings.merge!(Settings::SMTP.settings)
    end
  end

  private
  # only the App key keeps every mailer on the transactional path -- which makes
  # the credentials the deploy-time switch, and means the campaign can be built
  # before anything is pointed at it.
  def deliver_via_customerio_event?
    return false if @customerio_delivery_options&.dig(:customerio_event_name).blank?

    ForemInstance.customerio_track_enabled?
  end

  # The flag check and Customer.io identifiers both key off mail.to.first:
  # all Forem mailers are single-recipient today.
  def customerio_recipient
    return @customerio_recipient if defined?(@customerio_recipient)

    @customerio_recipient = User.find_by(email: mail.to.first.to_s.downcase)
  end

  # People in Customer.io are keyed by MLH Core user id (DEV profiles were
  # stitched via the dev:<id> anonymous id); fall back to email for
  # recipients without a linked Core account.
  def customerio_identifiers
    mlh_uid = customerio_recipient&.identities&.where(provider: "mlh")&.pick(:uid)
    return { id: mlh_uid } if mlh_uid.present?

    { email: mail.to.first }
  end
end

content.text:
The DEV↔MLH link exists; the two CIO profiles were created by a race at signup.

**What happened (siyadyusuf, DEV user 4136329, signed up via GitHub 2026-09-21 19:03:46 UTC):**

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 19:03:46 | DEV user created |
| 19:03:47 | DEV sends an email through CIO. There's no MLH identity yet, so `customerio_identifiers` falls back to `{ email: ... }` (`app/mailers/concerns/deliverable.rb:145`). CIO creates person `…f894d602` with **`id` = the email address** and no `email` attribute. |
| 19:03:50 | Core creates the shadow user `01a0c55a-…` and DEV stores it as the `mlh` identity. |
| 19:03:55 | Core syncs to CIO and creates person `…f994d602` with `id` = the Core UUID, `email` as a plain attribute, and `anonymous_id: dev:4136329`. |

**Why CIO didn't merge them:** the first profile's email is stored as its `id`, not in an email identifier. CIO only auto-merges when the same identifier value shows up again. The second profile's `id` is a different value (the Core UUID), and matching `email` attributes don't trigger a merge. So any new signup that gets a DEV email in the few seconds before Core links the account will probably end up with a duplicate like this.

**DEV admin:** the link is there. The identities are `github` and `mlh` = `01a0c55a-6041-4642-1e7d-77aa73dbf708`. It isn't shown at the top of the profile because that section only lists identities whose email differs from the account email (`_profile.html.erb:41`). You'll find it under More → Identities, or in the social accounts list under the profile actions. On Core the shadow is still unclaimed, which is expected.

**Fix options:**
1. **This person:** merge the two profiles with CIO's `POST /customers/merge`, keeping the UUID profile as primary. That's a write, so I'd stage it as a script for you to run.
2. **Stop it happening:** when Core creates a shadow, have it merge any existing CIO person whose `id` is that email. Or have DEV hold signup-time emails until the `mlh` identity exists. The Core-side merge is more reliable because it also cleans up any earlier duplicates.

This is the same race, with one difference: this person already had a claimed MLH account.

- **Saumya, DEV user 4136168:** the MLH account `01997c9b-…` has been claimed since Sep 2025. They signed up for DEV with Google on 2026-09-21 at 17:02:43 UTC. DEV sent an email while the user had no `mlh` identity yet, so CIO created `…8f92d602` with `id` = `saumyab1@umbc.edu` at 17:02:45. DEV didn't link to the existing MLH account until 17:04:39, two minutes later. After that, the MLH profile's `email` attribute matched, but CIO never merges on an attribute.
- **DEV admin:** the link is there too, as `mlh` = `01997c9b-bc4a-8472-f4e9-661bbaf80394`. It's hidden from the profile header for the same reason as the first user (same email), and it shows under More → Identities.

**Scope:** this probably affects nearly every new signup. Over the last 7 days, 11,269 of 11,389 DEV signups got their `mlh` identity *after* the user row was created, 32 seconds later on average. Any email sent in that window goes out keyed by email and leaves an orphan email-id profile. I'm inferring that from the timing; I haven't counted the duplicate profiles in CIO. The likely trigger is a signup-time mailer, since `confirmation_sent_at` is set when the user is created, even for OAuth signups.

**Fix:** the fallback in `customerio_identifiers` (`deliverable.rb:145`) is what creates the orphans. I'd do both of these:
1. **Core:** when it links or creates the MLH user for a DEV account, call CIO's merge with the email-id profile as the secondary. That also cleans up the existing duplicates as users re-sync.
2. **Backfill:** find CIO people whose `id` contains `@` and whose email matches a UUID-keyed person, then merge them. That's a write, so I'd stage it as a script for you to run.

module Trackers
  # Customer.io CDP (formerly Data Pipelines) adapter. The Pipelines API is
  # Segment-compatible; we use the analytics-ruby gem pointed at cdp.customer.io.
  #
  # Configure via ENV:
  #   CUSTOMERIO_CDP_WRITE_KEY  required; absence leaves the adapter disabled
  #   CUSTOMERIO_CDP_HOST       optional override; defaults to cdp.customer.io
  class CustomerioCdp < Base
    DEFAULT_HOST = "cdp.customer.io".freeze
    # Customer.io CDP does not implement analytics-ruby's default /v1/import
    # path (404); its Segment-compatible batch endpoint is /v1/batch.
    BATCH_PATH = "/v1/batch".freeze
    # Events that fire after the user row is destroyed. Straggler events for
    # deleted users are otherwise dropped (they could resurrect state after a
    # GDPR erasure), so these are the only ones that deliver without a live
    # row — possible because identity comes from the stable anonymous id and
    # the payload's own mlh_user_id, both knowable post-destruction.
    DESTRUCTIVE_EVENTS = ["user_gdpr_deleted"].freeze

    def enabled?
      # Resolve the setting via the default subforem (like mailers do): the admin
      # panel saves settings scoped to the request's subforem, and outside a request
      # (Sidekiq, console) a bare read would only see the global row.
      ApplicationConfig["CUSTOMERIO_CDP_WRITE_KEY"].present? &&
        Settings::General.customerio_cdp_enabled(subforem_id: Subforem.cached_default_id)
    end

    # Identity follows the Segment spec: every call carries a stable
    # anonymous_id ("dev:<DEV user id>"), plus user_id set to the canonical
    # MLH (Core) user id once the account is linked — sending both stitches
    # the pre-link anonymous history onto the person downstream. Email is
    # never an identity field; it travels in properties only.
    def track(event_name:, user_ids:, properties:, timestamp: nil)
      destructive = DESTRUCTIVE_EVENTS.include?(event_name)
      ids = deliverable_ids(Array.wrap(user_ids), destructive)
      # Send-time lookup so the link is current; for destructive events the
      # identity row died with the user, so the payload's pre-destruction
      # capture is the fallback.
      linked_uids = Identity.where(provider: "mlh", user_id: ids).pluck(:user_id, :uid).to_h

      event = Trackable::EventName.prefixed(event_name)

      ids.each do |id|
        attributes = {
          anonymous_id: "dev:#{id}",
          event: event,
          properties: properties,
          timestamp: timestamp
        }
        mlh_uid = linked_uids[id] || (properties["mlh_user_id"].presence if destructive)
        attributes[:user_id] = mlh_uid if mlh_uid
        client.track(attributes)
      end
    end

    private

    def deliverable_ids(ids, destructive)
      return ids if destructive

      User.where(id: ids).ids
    end

    def client
      @client ||= Segment::Analytics.new(
        write_key: ApplicationConfig["CUSTOMERIO_CDP_WRITE_KEY"],
        host: ApplicationConfig["CUSTOMERIO_CDP_HOST"].presence || DEFAULT_HOST,
        path: BATCH_PATH,
      )
    end
  end
end
# frozen_string_literal: true

# Merges a DEV (Forem) account's anonymous Customer.io profile (anonymous_id
# "dev:<forem id>") into its Core-identified person (user_id = Core id), so the
# user's pre-link anonymous engagement history is stitched onto their Core
# profile instead of stranded.
#
# DEV's CustomerioCdp adapter attaches user_id only once DEV holds the mlh
# link, so a user's first DEV events land on the anonymous "dev:<id>" profile
# and only stitch onto the person when a later DEV event carries both ids.
# This closes that gap on admission: User#identify_user enqueues this job for
# every not-yet-stitched DEV link, so live sync, the mass import, and a cold
# user's first gated identify all stitch through one path instead of waiting on
# the user's next DEV activity. On a successful identify the job stamps
# cio_stitched_at on the Dev profile so future identifies stop re-enqueuing it.
#
# The stitch is an `identify` carrying BOTH user_id and anonymous_id, NOT an
# `alias`. Our Segment "MLH Core" source feeds a Customer.io (Actions)
# destination, and Actions destinations only run configured Mappings: there is
# no Alias trigger there, so alias calls are accepted by Segment and then
# silently discarded at the destination ("Action missing mapping or trigger").
# The enabled Identify mapping already maps anonymousId -> Customer.io's
# Anonymous ID, which is the same path that merges anonymous web activity on
# sign-in (analytics.js identify auto-attaches anonymousId). Traits are
# intentionally omitted: person attributes are owned by User#identify_user, and
# the empty default keeps this a pure identity stitch that cannot clobber them.
#
# The link is re-verified at run time so a stale enqueue (GDPR delete,
# DEV-side merge, or Core-side re-point between enqueue and perform) never
# stitches the anonymous profile onto a dead or wrong Core user. Identifying is
# idempotent in Customer.io, so duplicate runs are harmless.
#
# A moderation or prune can also land between enqueue and perform: the moderate
# handler stamps moderation_status on the Dev profile and then prunes the CIO
# profile (setting cio_pruned_at) for spam/banished accounts. A stitch running
# after that CIO delete would re-mint the very profile the prune removed, so
# both are re-checked here and suppress the identify.
class StitchDevCioProfileJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :low

  def perform(forem_user_id, core_user_id:)
    profile = SocialProfiles::Dev.find_by(network_id: forem_user_id, user_id: core_user_id)
    return if profile.nil? || suppressed?(profile)

    $segment_client.identify(
      user_id: core_user_id,
      anonymous_id: SocialProfiles::Dev.cio_anonymous_id(forem_user_id)
    )
    stamp_stitched(profile)
  end

  private

  # A stitch identify mints a CIO person if none exists, so it must not run for
  # a moderated account or one whose CIO profile was just pruned.
  def suppressed?(profile)
    profile.custom_fields&.dig('moderation_status').present? ||
      profile.user&.cio_pruned_at.present?
  end

  # Marks the anonymous profile as stitched so User#identify_user stops
  # re-enqueuing this job for the link on the person's future identifies. A
  # custom_fields-only save does not trip SocialProfiles::Dev#cio_relevant_change?,
  # so this write does not re-identify the user and cannot loop back into this job.
  def stamp_stitched(profile)
    profile.update!(custom_fields: profile.custom_fields.to_h.merge('cio_stitched_at' => Time.current.iso8601))
  end
end
  def clear_stale_cio_pruned_at
    return if cio_pruned_at.nil?

    update_column(:cio_pruned_at, nil) # rubocop:disable Rails/SkipsModelValidations
  end

  def sync_topic_subscriptions
    PushUserSubscriptionPreferences.perform_later(self)
  end

  # Enqueue the anonymous->identified Customer.io stitch for any DEV link that
  # is not stitched yet, so a person's pre-link "dev:<id>" engagement history
  # merges onto their Core profile. This is the single admission point for the
  # stitch: live sync, the mass import, and a cold user's first gated identify
  # all reach it because a DEV link create/re-point re-identifies the user.
  #
  # Uses the plural query (not the has_one dev_profile) so a merged person
  # holding two DEV links gets each dev:<id> anonymous profile stitched on its
  # OWN one-shot identify — anonymous-profile merges are additive in CIO, and
  # the recurring traits identify above must never carry an anonymous_id or it
  # would re-assert one dev:<id> on every attribute change and stomp the web
  # source's anonymous_id writes. Duplicate enqueues before the stamp lands are
  # harmless: the stitch identify is idempotent in Customer.io.
  def stitch_dev_cio_profiles
    SocialProfiles::Dev.where(user_id: id).cio_unstitched.pluck(:network_id).each do |network_id|
      StitchDevCioProfileJob.perform_later(network_id, core_user_id: id)
    end
  end

  # A previously suppressed email that is registered again stays suppressed
  # until it is verified. Until then, do not sync user to Segment/Customer.io.
  def primary_email_suppressed?
    return false unless email.present?

    SuppressedIdentifier.suppressed?(email, SuppressedIdentifier::EMAIL)
  end
end

module DeliveryMethods
  # ActionMailer delivery method that hands the message to a Customer.io
  # event-triggered campaign instead of sending it. Selected per message by the
  # Deliverable concern when the mailer declares a customerio_event_name, the
  # Track API credentials are configured, and the :customerio_email_delivery
  # flag passes for the recipient.
  #
  # Rails still owns who, what and when; Customer.io owns rendering, sending and
  # conversion goals. Keeping ActionMailer in the loop is what makes that
  # affordable: AhoyEmail::Observer#delivered_email writes the ahoy_messages row
  # after any delivery method returns, so send counts and the digest's own
  # suppression gate keep working, and mail.ahoy_data is already populated by the
  # time deliver! runs, so the links inside the payload can be signed.
  #
  # Unlike the transactional path this is fire-and-forget from Rails' side: the
  # Track API accepting the event is not the same as Customer.io sending the
  # mail, which the campaign can still suppress afterwards. That divergence is
  # the reason the campaign is expected to carry exactly one suppression rule.
  class CustomerIoEvent
    attr_accessor :settings

    def initialize(delivery_method_options = {})
      self.settings = delivery_method_options
    end

    def deliver!(mail)
      # The gem does not wrap POST /v2/entity, but /v2/batch takes the same
      # entity objects and Customerio::Client#batch verifies the response, so a
      # rejected event raises here rather than being silently dropped -- which
      # is what keeps Ahoy from recording a row for a send that never happened.
      CUSTOMERIO_TRACK_API.batch([entity(mail)])
    end

    private

    def entity(mail)
      {
        type: "person",
        action: "event",
        # Resolved by Deliverable#customerio_identifiers, same as the
        # transactional path: the MLH Core uid where the account is linked,
        # falling back to email.
        identifiers: settings[:identifiers],
        # Mailers declare the bare event ("digest_ready"); the deploy's APP_NAME
        # is spliced in here, at the boundary, exactly as the CDP adapter does.
        # The campaign's trigger has to match the namespaced name.
        name: Trackable::EventName.prefixed(settings[:customerio_event_name]),
        attributes: attributes(mail)
      }
    end

    # Defaults are a floor, not a ceiling: message_data may override either.
    # recipient is set explicitly because the Customer.io profile is keyed on the
    # MLH person, whose primary address is not necessarily the DEV one -- the
    # campaign addresses the mail to {{event.recipient}}.
    def attributes(mail)
      {
        "recipient" => mail.to&.first,
        "subject" => mail.subject
      }.merge(tracked_message_data(mail))
    end

    # Customer.io renders from the event payload, so Ahoy's link rewriting --
    # which operates on the ActionMailer body -- never reaches the recipient.
    # Re-apply it here for the same reason DeliveryMethods::CustomerIo does.
    def tracked_message_data(mail)
      return {} if settings[:message_data].blank?

      Emails::AhoyLinkDecorator.call(settings[:message_data], ahoy_data: mail.ahoy_data)
    end
  end
end
module DeliveryMethods
  # ActionMailer delivery method that sends through the Customer.io App API
  # (transactional messages) instead of SMTP. Selected per message by the
  # Deliverable concern when CUSTOMERIO_APP_KEY is configured and the
  # :customerio_email_delivery flag passes for the recipient.
  class CustomerIo
    attr_accessor :settings

    DEFAULTS = {
      tracked: true
    }.freeze

    # Customer.io renders the message itself, so headers set on the Mail object
    # are not carried over unless we forward them explicitly. RFC 8058
    # one-click unsubscribe only works if these reach the recipient.
    FORWARDED_HEADERS = %w[List-Unsubscribe List-Unsubscribe-Post].freeze

    def initialize(delivery_method_options = {})
      self.settings = DEFAULTS.merge(delivery_method_options)
    end

    def deliver!(mail)
      request = Customerio::SendEmailRequest.new(build_message(mail))
      mail.attachments.each do |attachment|
        request.attach(attachment.filename, attachment.body.to_s)
      end

      CUSTOMERIO_API.send_email(request)
    end

    private

    def build_message(mail)
      {}.tap do |message|
        # With a transactional_message_id the Customer.io template renders the
        # content; without one this is a body passthrough send. The App API
        # treats body/from in the request as overrides of what the template
        # already defines, so the template's own sender identity only survives
        # if we leave both out.
        unless settings[:transactional_message_id]
          message[:body] = build_body(mail)
          message[:from] = mail.from.first if mail.from
        end
        message[:subject] = mail.subject if mail.subject
        message[:identifiers] = { email: mail.to.first } if mail.to
        message[:reply_to] = mail.reply_to.first if mail.reply_to
        message[:to] = mail.to.join(",") if mail.to
        forwarded = forwarded_headers(mail)
        message[:headers] = forwarded if forwarded.any?
      end.merge(settings).merge(tracked_message_data(mail))
    end

    # Customer.io renders from message_data, so Ahoy's link rewriting -- which
    # operates on the ActionMailer body -- never reaches the recipient. Re-apply
    # it to the payload so clicks still reach Ahoy::EmailClicksController.
    #
    # mail.ahoy_data is set by AhoyEmail::Processor in an after_action. Rails
    # runs after_actions in reverse registration order, so it lands *after*
    # Deliverable#set_delivery_options picks this delivery method -- which is
    # why the token is read here at delivery time rather than captured into
    # settings when the delivery method was chosen.
    def tracked_message_data(mail)
      return {} if settings[:message_data].blank?

      { message_data: Emails::AhoyLinkDecorator.call(settings[:message_data], ahoy_data: mail.ahoy_data) }
    end

    def forwarded_headers(mail)
      FORWARDED_HEADERS.each_with_object({}) do |name, headers|
        value = mail[name]&.value
        headers[name] = value if value.present?
      end
    end

    # Customer.io's body field is HTML. Prefer the html_part (Mail searches
    # nested multipart structures recursively), falling back to the text part
    # or the raw body for single-part mail.
    def build_body(mail)
      part = mail.html_part || mail.text_part
      (part || mail).body.to_s
    end
  end
end

You're right, but only for tracking events. `dev:<id>` goes out on the CDP event path. Email sends take a separate path, and that path can't carry it.

**Tracking events (anonymous id works):**
- **DEV:** `Trackers::CustomerioCdp#track` (`app/services/trackers/customerio_cdp.rb:44`) always sends `anonymous_id: "dev:<id>"`, and adds `user_id` = the MLH uid once the link exists.
- **Core:** once it links the DEV account, `User#stitch_dev_cio_profiles` enqueues `StitchDevCioProfileJob`. That job sends an identify with both `user_id` = Core id and `anonymous_id` = `dev:<id>`, which merges the anonymous profile. It worked for both people: each UUID profile has `anonymous_id: dev:4136329` / `dev:4136168`.

**Email sends (anonymous id missing):**
- `Deliverable#customerio_identifiers` (`app/mailers/concerns/deliverable.rb:145`) sends `{ id: mlh_uid }`, or falls back to `{ email: }` when there's no link yet. It feeds both mail paths:
  - `DeliveryMethods::CustomerIo` (App API, transactional)
  - `DeliveryMethods::CustomerIoEvent` (Track API `/v2/batch` entity)
- Neither API accepts an anonymous id; they only take `id`, `email` or `cio_id`. So `dev:<id>` isn't a drop-in fix here.
- Our workspace is set to identify people by ID only, so CIO stored `{ email: }` as the person's **`id`** (`id: "siyadyusuf@outlook.com"`). Core's later identify uses `id` = UUID, which doesn't match. Nothing ever connects the two:
  - The stitch job only merges the `dev:<id>` anonymous profile.
  - A matching `email` attribute doesn't trigger a merge in ID-only mode.
- Both users got a DEV email before the MLH link existed: 1s before for the first user, about 2 min for the second. Over the last 7 days the link landed 32s after signup on average, so this probably hits most new signups that get a signup-time email.

**Fix options:**
1. **Core (recommended):** in `StitchDevCioProfileJob`, also merge the email-keyed person into the Core person with CIO's `POST /customers/merge`. It runs once per link, so it also cleans up duplicates for existing links if you re-run it over them.
2. **DEV:** don't send `{ email: }` for users who are about to be linked. That means delaying signup-time mail until the `mlh` identity exists, which is riskier because confirmation emails can't really wait.
3. **Workspace setting:** switching to "email or ID" would make Core's identify attach to the email person automatically. It's a workspace-wide change, so treat it as a separate decision.

Not with the APIs email goes through. Both email paths only accept `id`, `email` or `cio_id` as the person identifier:

- **Transactional (App API):** `SendEmailRequest` requires `identifiers`. The gem's `IdentifierType` allows only ID, CIOID and EMAIL (`customerio-6.1.0/lib/customerio/client.rb:303`).
- **Event-triggered (Track API `/v2` entity):** it takes the same three identifiers.

Anonymous id only exists on the CDP identify/track calls and on Track API anonymous events. Neither can address a transactional send to a person.

**What's possible with the same "dev id" key:**
1. **Send `{ id: "dev:<id>" }` instead of `{ email: }` for unlinked users.** The orphan would then have a predictable id instead of an email. But CIO treats a person `id` and an `anonymous_id` as different things, so Core's existing stitch identify still wouldn't merge it. Core would need one extra call in `StitchDevCioProfileJob`: `POST /customers/merge` with primary `{id: core_uuid}` and secondary `{id: "dev:<id>"}`. It stays a two-repo change, but the criteria match the existing stitch exactly, with no email-lookup ambiguity.
2. **Anonymous events for the event-triggered path only.** Send `anonymous_id: "dev:<id>"` plus a `recipient`, and the existing stitch identify merges it. That doesn't help transactional sends, and I'm not sure CIO lets an anonymous event with an anonymous_id trigger a campaign send; I'd need to check the docs.

Option 1 is the closest to what you're after: DEV changes one line in `customerio_identifiers`, and Core adds one merge call next to the stitch it already does. Want me to draft both?

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Tmp
  # Deletes Customer.io person profiles in bulk via the Track v2 /batch
  # endpoint — the customerio gem only wraps the one-person-per-request v1
  # API, which is hours of round trips at backfill-prune scale (~520K).
  # Same delete-then-let-caller-stamp semantics as UserPruningService:
  # a failed request raises Customerio::InvalidResponse before any
  # cio_pruned_at bookkeeping, so re-runs pick the same users back up
  # (deletes are idempotent on the Customer.io side).
  class CioBatchDeleter < ApplicationService
    include Customerio::RateLimitRetryable

    # The v2 batch endpoint caps the request payload at 500KB; a
    # person-delete command is ~70 bytes, so 1,000 stays well clear.
    MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 1_000

    attr_reader :user_ids

    def initialize(user_ids:)
      raise ArgumentError, "user_ids exceeds MAX_BATCH_SIZE (#{MAX_BATCH_SIZE})" if user_ids.size > MAX_BATCH_SIZE

      @user_ids = user_ids
      super
    end

    def call!
      with_rate_limit_retry do
        client.request_and_verify_response(:post, '/api/v2/batch', batch: delete_commands)
      end
    end

    private

    def delete_commands
      user_ids.map { |id| { type: 'person', identifiers: { id: }, action: 'delete' } }
    end

    def client
      Customerio::BaseClient.new(
        { site_id: ENV.fetch('CUSTOMERIO_SITE_ID', nil), api_key: ENV.fetch('CUSTOMERIO_APP_SECRET', nil) },
        url: Customerio::Regions::US.track_url
      )
    end
  end
end

module SocialProfiles
  class Dev < ::SocialProfile
    # Whether the profile is destroyed on its own (bad-link cleanup) or via
    # the user's dependent: :destroy cascade, DEV must drop the mlh identity
    # that pointed at this Core link - otherwise it dangles at a dead id.
    # When the link is re-pointed at a different Core user (a DEV-side merge
    # moves the anonymous "dev:<id>" profile onto the surviving person), the
    # old cio_stitched_at stamp is stale: the anonymous profile now belongs to
    # a different user and must re-stitch. Drop the stamp so the reidentify
    # this same save triggers (user_id change trips cio_relevant_change?)
    # re-enqueues StitchDevCioProfileJob for the surviving user.
    before_update :clear_cio_stitched_stamp, if: :will_save_change_to_user_id?

    # Whether the profile is destroyed on its own (bad-link cleanup) or via
    # the user's dependent: :destroy cascade, DEV must drop the mlh identity
    # that pointed at this Core link - otherwise it dangles at a dead id.
    after_commit :unlink_dev_identity, on: :destroy

    # Push the DEV username/id (person-level CIO attributes on the user
    # serializer) to Customer.io whenever this link is created or a relevant
    # field changes. On create the network id/username/user id all register as
    # saved changes (nil -> value), so the single cio_relevant_change? guard
    # covers create too while a no-op save (backfill re-run with unchanged
    # fields) or a custom_fields-only update does not re-identify. Gated on the
    # in-memory allow_cio_triggers of the linked user, so the ~770K
    # non-actively-emailed backfill users and moderated / opted-out users never
    # get a CIO profile minted.
    after_commit :reidentify_core_user, on: [:create, :update], if: :cio_relevant_change?

    # Grant any badges that were previously earned
    after_create_commit :retry_badge_entitlements

    # DEV links whose anonymous Customer.io profile has not been stitched onto
    # the Core person yet — custom_fields lacks the cio_stitched_at stamp
    # StitchDevCioProfileJob writes on a successful identify. Used by
    # User#identify_user to lazily stitch a person's DEV links on admission.
    scope :cio_unstitched, -> { where("custom_fields->>'cio_stitched_at' IS NULL") }

    # Resolves the Core user behind a DEV (Forem) account, in trust order:
    # the MyMLH OAuth uid (a deterministic Core id, merge-aware), then the
    # Dev social profile link, then a claimed/primary email match. Email
    # matching deliberately stops at identify_user_by - an address that
    # exists only as an unclaimed secondary identifier is too weak a link
    # to attach DEV data to, so callers create a fresh user instead and the
    # MyMLH claim flow merges the two if the person later proves ownership.
    # Shared resolution for every DEV ingest path (live sync handler; the
    # since-removed one-off backfill import used it too).
    #
    # `email` is nil-safe, and callers are expected to pass nil for an address
    # they cannot treat as proof of identity: the live DEV sync passes nil for
    # an UNCONFIRMED DEV address, because matching on one would attach an
    # attacker's DEV account to whoever actually owns that mailbox.
    def self.resolve_core_user(forem_user_id:, email:, mlh_user_id: nil)
      User.resolve_with_merges(mlh_user_id) ||
        find_by(network_id: forem_user_id)&.user ||
        Email.identify_user_by(email)
    end

    # The Customer.io anonymous_id that DEV's Trackers::CustomerioCdp adapter
    # tags every event with. DEV sends it on its own (without a user_id) until
    # it holds the mlh identity link, so a DEV account's pre-link engagement
    # lands on this anonymous profile. Stitching that history onto the Core
    # person means identifying with this as the anonymous_id. Owned here so the
    # single-link and bulk stitch jobs cannot drift from DEV's format.
    def self.cio_anonymous_id(forem_user_id)
      "dev:#{forem_user_id}"
    end

    private

    def unlink_dev_identity
      UnlinkDevCoreLinkJob.perform_later(network_id, core_user_id: user_id)
    end

    def retry_badge_entitlements
      user.entitlements.dev_badge
        .where.not(status: Entitlement.statuses[:assigned])
        .find_each(&:retry!)
    end

    def clear_cio_stitched_stamp
      self.custom_fields = custom_fields.to_h.except('cio_stitched_at')
    end

    # The linked user's create-time identify may have run before this profile
    # existed and cached a nil dev_profile; reset the association so the
    # serializer re-reads the now-committed link and sends the DEV attributes.
    def reidentify_core_user
      return unless user&.allow_cio_triggers

      user.association(:dev_profile).reset
      user.identify_user
    end

    # True on create (network id/username/user id go nil -> value) and on an
    # update that touches any of those; false for a no-op or custom_fields-only
    # save.

    def cio_relevant_change?
      saved_change_to_network_username? || saved_change_to_network_id? || saved_change_to_user_id?
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

# One-off rename of the DEV digest Customer.io subscription topic in
# users.topic_subscriptions, from the superseded identifier to the current one
# (topic_11 -> topic_29 at the time of writing; both come from
# CustomerIoTopic's :dev_digest role, never from a literal here).
#
# Customer.io restructured its subscription center and the DEV digest moved to
# a new topic id. Core stores consent keyed by that id, so ~978k rows still
# carry it under the old key. Readers already fall back through the legacy
# identifier (CustomerIoTopic.identifiers_for), which is what makes the rollout
# safe; this job retires that fallback by moving the data.
#
# ORDERING: run this only AFTER the deploy that introduced the fallback has
# fully rolled out. Until then old workers still write the legacy key, and a
# row renamed before its writer was replaced can be re-created under the old
# key. Nothing is lost if that happens — the fallback still reads it and a
# rerun picks it up — but a clean rollout avoids the churn.
#
# Set-based: one UPDATE per batch, no per-row ActiveRecord loads, so the
# after_commit callbacks (identify_user, sync_topic_subscriptions,
# push_dev_newsletter_state) do NOT fire. That is deliberate — this relabels
# Core's local copy of consent that Customer.io already holds under the new
# topic, so there is nothing to push back, and firing callbacks would mean
# ~978k identifies and DEV pushes for a no-op change. updated_at is likewise
# left alone so the rename does not masquerade as user activity.
#
# Idempotent and resumable: the scope only matches rows that still carry the
# legacy key, so a retry or re-enqueue picks up where it left off.
#
# One-off Tmp job (delete once the rename is verified, together with the
# `legacy_ids` entry in config/customer_io_topics.yml): enqueue from the
# console.
#
#   Tmp::RenameDevDigestTopicJob.perform_later                 # dry-run
#   Tmp::RenameDevDigestTopicJob.perform_later(dry_run: false) # rename
module Tmp
  class RenameDevDigestTopicJob < ApplicationJob
    queue_as :low

    BATCH_SIZE = 1_000
    THROTTLE_SECONDS = 0.1
    SAMPLE_SIZE = 5

    def perform(dry_run: true)
      @dry_run = dry_run

      log_sample
      renamed = dry_run ? legacy_rows.count : rename_all
      log_result(renamed)
    end

    private

    attr_reader :dry_run

    def current_identifier
      @current_identifier ||= CustomerIoTopic.identifier_for(:dev_digest)
    end

# frozen_string_literal: true

# Pushes the Core user id for a DEV (Forem) account back to DEV as an mlh
# identity via DEV's admin identities API, so DEV holds the reverse link
# without requiring the user to OAuth. Enqueued whenever a Dev social
# profile is newly created or re-pointed, and by import:push_dev_core_links
# for the backfill.
#
# Args are primitives (not the profile record): the link can vanish or move
# between enqueue and perform - GDPR deletes, DEV-side merges, Core-side
# re-points - and a GlobalID of a destroyed profile would burn every retry
# on deserialization. Instead the job re-checks that the link is still
# current at run time and no-ops when it isn't, so a stale enqueue can
# never write a dead link to DEV.
#
# DEV's endpoint is idempotent (200 already_linked on repeats). Only
# failures a retry can actually fix raise: rate limits (429), server errors
# (5xx), network failures, and auth failures (401/403 from an expired or
# revoked DEV_API_KEY). Every other 4xx is permanent for this payload, so it
# is logged and dropped rather than burning the whole retry schedule - a
# deleted DEV account (404), a rejected payload (422), and conflicts (409)
# alike. The one exception is a 409 where the DEV account holds a stale mlh
# identity from a Core-side merge, which is unlinked and re-linked.
class PushDevCoreLinkJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :low

  def perform(forem_user_id, core_user_id:)
    return if ENV['DEV_API_KEY'].blank?

    @forem_user_id = forem_user_id
    @core_user_id = core_user_id
    return unless current_link?

    push_identity_link
  end

  private

  attr_reader :forem_user_id, :core_user_id

  def current_link?
    SocialProfiles::Dev.exists?(network_id: forem_user_id, user_id: core_user_id)
  end

  # Unrescued errors (429, 401, 403, and network failures) propagate so
  # Sidekiq retries them.
  def push_identity_link
    link_identity
  rescue Forem::NotFoundError, Forem::InvalidRequestError => e
    log_dropped_error(e)
  rescue Forem::ConflictError => e
    handle_conflict(e)
  rescue Forem::APIError => e
    # APIError covers both 5xx and any status without a dedicated subclass
    # (400, 410, ...); only the server-side half is worth retrying.
    raise if server_error?(e)

    log_dropped_error(e)
  end

  def server_error?(error)
    error.http_status.to_i >= 500
  end

  def handle_conflict(error)
    return replace_stale_identity if stale_identity_conflict?(error)

    log_dropped_error(error)
  end

  def link_identity
    client.admin_users.link_identity(
      forem_user_id,
      provider: 'mlh',
      uid: core_user_id
    )
  end

  def client
    @client ||= Forem.client

module DataUpdateScripts
  class ReprocessMarkdownFeedImports
    FETCH_TIMEOUT = 20
    FEED_USER_AGENT = "Forem/1.0 (+https://forem.com; RSS Feed Fetcher)".freeze

    def run
      log("Starting reprocessing of markdown feed imports...")

      draft_feed_articles = Article.where(published_from_feed: true, published: false)
      total = draft_feed_articles.count
      log("Found #{total} draft feed-imported articles")

      return if total.zero?

      # Group articles by their feed source to batch re-fetches
      articles_by_feed = group_articles_by_feed_source(draft_feed_articles)
      log("Grouped into #{articles_by_feed.size} unique feeds")

      fixed = 0
      skipped = 0
      errored = 0

      articles_by_feed.each do |feed_url, articles|
        feed = fetch_and_parse_feed(feed_url)
        unless feed
          log("  Could not fetch/parse feed: #{feed_url}, skipping #{articles.size} articles")
          skipped += articles.size
          next
        end

        entries_by_url = index_entries_by_url(feed)

        articles.each do |article|
          entry = entries_by_url[article.feed_source_url]
          unless entry
            skipped += 1
            next
          end

          content = entry.content || entry.summary
          if content.blank? || html_content?(content)
            skipped += 1
            next
          end

          # This article had markdown content that was mangled by the HTML pipeline.
          # Re-assemble the body markdown using the fixed code.
          source = find_feed_source(article, feed_url)
          new_markdown = Feeds::AssembleArticleMarkdown.call(
            entry, article.user, feed, article.feed_source_url, feed_source: source
          )
          article.update!(body_markdown: new_markdown)
          fixed += 1
        rescue StandardError => e
          log("  Error reprocessing article #{article.id}: #{e.message}")
          errored += 1
        end
      end

      log("Completed: #{fixed} fixed, #{skipped} skipped, #{errored} errors (of #{total} total)")
    end

    private

    def group_articles_by_feed_source(articles)
      result = {}

      articles.find_each do |article|
        # Try to find the feed URL via Feeds::Source
        source = Feeds::Source.joins(import_logs: :import_items)
          .where(feed_import_items: { article_id: article.id })
          .first

        # Fall back to deriving the feed URL from the article's feed_source_url domain
        feed_url = source&.feed_url
        unless feed_url
          # Try matching by user's feed sources
          source = Feeds::Source.where(user_id: article.user_id).first
          feed_url = source&.feed_url
        end

        next unless feed_url

        result[feed_url] ||= []
        result[feed_url] << article
      end

      result
    end

    def fetch_and_parse_feed(url)
      response = HTTParty.get(url,
                              timeout: FETCH_TIMEOUT,
                              headers: { "User-Agent" => FEED_USER_AGENT })
      Feedjira.parse(response.body)
    rescue StandardError => e
      log("  Fetch/parse error for #{url}: #{e.class} - #{e.message}")
      nil
    end

    def index_entries_by_url(feed)
      feed.entries.index_by { |e| e.url.to_s.strip.split("?source=")[0] }
    end

    def find_feed_source(article, feed_url)

module DataUpdateScripts
  # Before Deliverable keyed unlinked recipients as "dev:<id>", mail sent to a
  # new user before their mlh identity landed was keyed by email. Customer.io
  # stored that address as the person's id, leaving an orphan profile beside
  # the one keyed by the MLH uid that nothing ever merges. Merge each orphan
  # into its linked person.
  #
  # Scoped to users linked after signup since Customer.io delivery shipped
  # (2026-07-16) -- the only accounts that could have been mailed unlinked.
  # A merge whose secondary does not exist is a no-op on Customer.io's side, so
  # users who were never mailed before linking are harmless to include.
  class MergeEmailKeyedCustomerioProfiles
    ROLLOUT_DATE = Time.zone.parse("2026-07-16")
    # /v2/batch caps a request at 500KB; a merge op is ~150 bytes.
    BATCH_SIZE = 1_000

    def run
      return unless ForemInstance.customerio_track_enabled?

      identities.in_batches(of: BATCH_SIZE) do |batch|
        ops = batch.pluck("identities.uid", "users.email").filter_map do |uid, email|
          next if email.blank?

          { type: "person", action: "merge", primary: { id: uid }, secondary: { id: email } }
        end
        CUSTOMERIO_TRACK_API.batch(ops) if ops.any?
      end
    end

    private

    def identities
      Identity.joins(:user)
        .where(provider: "mlh")
        .where(users: { created_at: ROLLOUT_DATE.. })
        .where("identities.created_at > users.created_at")
    end
  end
end

---
name: forem-local-dev-env-gotchas
description: Two silent Forem local-dev traps — pg/libpq GSS segfault in forked Puma workers on macOS, and strong_migrations 1.8 making rails db:migrate a no-op on Rails 8
metadata:
  type: project
---

Local Forem dev (macOS, Aug 2026) has two failures that look like config loss but are not:

1. **Puma workers segfault on every DB request.** The precompiled `pg-1.6.3-arm64-darwin` gem bundles libpq 18, whose `PQconnectStart` → `pg_GSS_have_cred_cache` → Kerberos/Heimdal → CoreFoundation call is not fork-safe. With `preload_app!` + `WEB_CONCURRENCY=2` in `config/puma.rb`, every forked worker dies with SIGSEGV. Fix: `PGGSSENCMODE=disable` in `.env` (added 2026-08-27). Non-forked `PG.connect` works fine, which is why it only shows up under the server.

2. **`rails db:migrate` silently runs nothing** and just prints "Dumping schema". `strong_migrations` is pinned `~> 1.7` in the Gemfile → resolves to 1.8.0, whose `DatabaseTasks#migrate(*args)` override drops keyword args; Rails 8's `migrate_all` calls `migrate(skip_initialize: true)`, so that hash lands in the `version` slot and the filter block matches no migration. Upstream fixed it in strong_migrations 2.0.2 ("Fixed migrations not running with Active Record 8"). Until the Gemfile is bumped to `~> 2.0`, migrate one at a time with `rails db:migrate:up VERSION=...`.

3. **Schema dumps drop unrelated columns/indexes.** Because of (2), the local DB is usually behind on recent migrations, so `db:migrate:up` re-dumps `schema.rb` without them (seen 2026-09-04: lost `favorited_weight`, `index_articles_on_published_at_and_score`, a recommended_articles_lists index). After any migration: `git checkout db/schema.rb`, then hand-add only the version bump and your own change, per AGENTS.md.

Also: ruby is pinned 3.4.9 by `~/Documents/GitHub/mise.toml`, which overrides Forem's `.ruby-version` (3.3.0); `forem/.mise.toml` now sets `ruby = "3.3.0"`. Forem runs on port 3006 behind Caddy (`forem.mlh.test`), see [[forem-fork-hygiene]].

# Merges the Customer.io person DEV (Forem) mints for a user mailed before the
# DEV<->Core link exists into the Core-identified person.
#
# DEV's CDP events carry "dev:<forem id>" as an anonymous_id, which
# StitchDevCioProfileJob's identify stitches. DEV's email sends cannot carry an
# anonymous_id (the App and Track entity APIs only take id/email/cio_id), so
# signup-time mail keys the recipient as a person with id "dev:<forem id>".
# An identify never merges two identified people, so this job merges them
# explicitly via the Track API.
#
# Enqueued by StitchDevCioProfileJob with a delay: Customer.io requires the
# primary to exist, and the Core person is minted by the Segment identify
# that just ran, asynchronously. Most DEV users are never mailed before
# linking, so a missing secondary is the common case; /v2/batch reports it as
# a per-op error in a 207, which the client treats as success.
class MergeDevCioPersonJob < ApplicationJob
  include Customerio::RateLimitRetryable

  queue_as :low

  # ponytail: fixed delay covers Segment->CIO latency and DEV's ~30s link lag;
  # mail DEV sends after this fires would re-mint the dev:<id> person.
  DELAY = 10.minutes

  def perform(forem_user_id, core_user_id:)
    profile = SocialProfiles::Dev.find_by(network_id: forem_user_id, user_id: core_user_id)
    return if profile.nil? || profile.user&.cio_pruned_at.present?

    with_rate_limit_retry do
      $cio_track_api.batch([
        {
          type: 'person',
          action: 'merge',
          primary: { id: core_user_id },
          secondary: { id: SocialProfiles::Dev.cio_anonymous_id(forem_user_id) }
        }
      ])
    end
  end
end

Both repos are changed and their specs pass. Nothing is committed yet.

**forem** (branch `cio-dev-id-fallback`):
- **Emails now use `dev:<id>`:** `customerio_identifiers` (`app/mailers/concerns/deliverable.rb:145`) keys a DEV user without an MLH link as `{ id: "dev:<id>" }`, not by email. Recipients who aren't DEV users still fall back to `{ email: }`. The two spec expectations in `spec/mailers/concerns/deliverable_spec.rb` are updated.
- **Cleanup script:** `lib/data_update_scripts/20260922120000_merge_email_keyed_customerio_profiles.rb` runs on deploy.
  - It covers users created since 2026-07-16 whose MLH link was created after they signed up; DEV prod shows about 105k.
  - For each, it merges the email-keyed profile `{id: users.email}` into the MLH profile `{id: uid}`, sent in `/v2/batch` calls of 1,000 merges.
  - Most of those users never got an email before linking, so they have no orphan. CIO reports those merges as per-item errors in a 207, which the gem counts as success, so they don't fail the run.
  - I checked the 207 behaviour against CIO's docs and the gem, not against the live API.
  - It has a new spec.

**mlh-core** (worktree `../mlh-core-cio-merge`, branch `cio-merge-dev-keyed-person` off `origin/main`, so your checkout is untouched):
- **New `MergeDevCioPersonJob`:** it merges `{id: "dev:<id>"}` into `{id: core_user_id}` through the Track `/v2/batch` merge, with Core's existing rate-limit retry. It re-checks the DEV link first, so an outdated job doesn't merge into the wrong person.
- **Wired into the stitch:** `StitchDevCioProfileJob` enqueues it 10 minutes after the stitch runs, so it's decided by the same thing as the anonymous-id stitch. CIO requires the MLH profile to already exist, and it's created asynchronously via Segment, hence the delay.

**Deploy Core first.** If forem goes first, new `dev:<id>` profiles pile up with nothing merging them until Core ships. If Core goes first, the merges just find nothing to merge.

**Known limit:** an email DEV sends after the 10-minute merge has run, while it still has no MLH link, would create a new `dev:<id>` profile. Given the ~30s average link time that should be rare; it's marked with a `ponytail:` comment in the job.

class PasswordlessMailer < ApplicationMailer
  CIO_PASSWORDLESS_TEMPLATE_ID = 'v4_my_mlh_sign_in'

  helper_method :magic_link

  def sign_in_email
    @otp = params[:otp]
    @user = params[:user]
    @sgid = params[:sgid]
    @email = params[:email].presence || @user.primary_email.identifier

    mail(
      to: @email,
      delivery_method_options: {
        transactional_message_id: CIO_PASSWORDLESS_TEMPLATE_ID,
        identifiers: {
          id: @user.id
        },
        message_data: {
          magic_link:,
          otp: @otp.plaintext
        }
      }
    )
  end

  private

  def magic_link
    base = URI.parse(Rails.application.config.auth_base_url)
    Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.web_auth_sign_in_magic_link_url(
      token: @sgid.to_s,
      host: base.host,
      protocol: base.scheme,
      port: base.port
    )
  end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module DeliveryMethods
  class CustomerIo
    attr_accessor :settings

    DEFAULTS = {
      tracked: true
    }.freeze

    def initialize(delivery_method_options)
      self.settings = DEFAULTS.merge(delivery_method_options)
    end

    def deliver!(mail)
      message = build_message(mail)

      request = Customerio::SendEmailRequest.new(message)
      if mail.attachments.present?
        mail.attachments.each do |attachment|
          request.attach(attachment.filename, attachment.body.to_s)
        end
      end

      response = CUSTOMERIO_API.send_email(request)
      capture_delivery_id(mail, response)
      response
    end

    private

    # Record the delivery_id Customer.io returns as the recipient's in-flight
    # (sent) deliverability event, so an inbound bounce/spam/delivered webhook
    # can be correlated back to this exact send. The message is already accepted;
    # capture is best-effort and must never turn a successful send into a job
    # failure (which would re-send), so DB/lookup errors are logged and swallowed
    # here rather than propagated.
    def capture_delivery_id(mail, response)
      delivery_id = response.is_a?(Hash) ? (response['delivery_id'] || response[:delivery_id]) : nil
      return if delivery_id.blank?

      email = recipient_email(mail)
      return unless email

      NotificationDeliverabilityEvent.record_sent!(identifier: email, channel: :email, delivery_id:)
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.error("[customerio_deliverability] delivery_id capture failed: #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
    end

    def recipient_email(mail)
      recipient = mail.to&.first
      return if recipient.blank?

      # Email downcases identifiers on write, so match on the normalized address.
      # Prefer the claimed (canonical) row over any unclaimed duplicate so capture
      # and inbound bounce ingestion resolve to the same identifier.
      scope = Email.where(identifier: recipient.downcase)
      scope.find_by(claimed: true) || scope.order(:created_at).first
    end

    def build_message(mail)
      {}.tap do |m|
        m[:body] = build_body(mail) unless settings[:transactional_message_id]
        m[:from] = mail.from.first if mail.from
        m[:subject] = mail.subject if mail.subject
        m[:identifiers] = { email: mail.to.first } if mail.to
        m[:reply_to] = mail.reply_to.first if mail.reply_to
        m[:to] = mail.to.join(',') if mail.to
      end
        .merge(settings)
    end

    def build_body(mail)
      if mail.body.parts.length > 1
        mail.body.parts.first.body.to_s
      else
        mail.body.to_s
      end
    end
  end
end

module Auth
  class SendPasswordlessSignInEmailJob < Auth::BaseEmailJob
    queue_as :high

    def perform(otp, email = nil)
      return if otp.sent?

      user = otp.user

      if email.blank?
        Rails.logger.warn("Auth::SendPasswordlessSignInEmailJob called without email parameter for OTP #{otp.id}")
        email = user.primary_email.identifier
      end

      sgid = user.to_sgid(expires_in: OneTimePassword::DEFAULT_EXPIRATION_TIME, for: 'sign_in')

      otp.regenerate
      otp.expires_at = OneTimePassword::DEFAULT_EXPIRATION_TIME.from_now

      ::PasswordlessMailer.with(
        otp:,
        user:,
        sgid:,
        email: email
      ).sign_in_email.deliver_now

      otp.sent_at = Time.current
      otp.save!
    end

    # Prefer the identifier captured at OTP creation. Falls back to
    # primary_email for in-flight OTPs that predate user_identifier_id
    # and for any future caller that doesn't stamp the column.
    def identifier
      otp = arguments.first
      otp.user_identifier || otp.user.primary_email
    end
  end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Web
  module Auth
    module Sessions
      class PasswordlessSignInService < ApplicationService
        attr_reader :email, :request

        def initialize(email:, request:)
          @email = email&.strip&.downcase
          @request = request

          super()
        end

        def call!
          validate_email!

          user = find_or_create_user
          raise_if_suspended(user)
          raise_if_discarded(user)

          otp = send_sign_in_email(user)

          { email: @email, otp: otp }
        end

        private

        def validate_email!
          return if @email.present?

          raise ArgumentError, I18n.t('web.auth.sessions.errors.email_required')
        end

        def find_or_create_user
          UserIdentifier.identify_user_by(@email) ||
            User.create!(primary_email_attributes: {
              identifier: @email,
              primary: true,
              skip_suppression_check: true
            })
        end

        def raise_if_suspended(user)
          return unless user.suspended?

          raise Errorable::Forbidden, I18n.t('web.auth.sessions.errors.account_suspended')
        end

        # A discarded user found by identifier means that account deletion is in
        # progress, i.e. the old identifier has not yet been suppressed but the
        # user record has been soft-deleted, so raise to prevent sign-ins.
        # Once account deletion is finalized, the identifier will be created
        # again (`skip_suppression_check: true` above) along with a fresh user,
        # so this will not raise.
        def raise_if_discarded(user)
          return unless user.discarded?

          raise Errorable::Forbidden, I18n.t('web.auth.sessions.errors.account_deleted')
        end

        def send_sign_in_email(user)
          identifier = user.emails.find_by(identifier: @email) || user.primary_email
          otp = OneTimePassword.create!(user: user, purpose: 'sign_in', user_identifier: identifier)
          ::Auth::SendPasswordlessSignInEmailJob.perform_later(otp, @email)
          otp
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

content.text:
I dropped the `dev:<id>` approach. Nothing is committed yet.

**What Core does:** it never emails someone who doesn't have a real person record. `PasswordlessSignInService#find_or_create_user` creates the unclaimed Core user synchronously, and every Core mailer then sends with `identifiers: { id: @user.id }`.

**What was actually causing the orphans:** both came from CIO transactional message 50, `dev_confirmation_instructions` ("confirm your DEV Community account"), sent within a second of signup. Both users had signed up with OAuth and were already confirmed. Forem's `User#confirmation_required?` override (from 2021) returns `ForemInstance.smtp_enabled?` and drops Devise's `!confirmed?` check. So every OAuth signup gets a pointless confirmation email before Core has linked the account. OAuth signups are 82% of volume: 9,333 of 11,398 in the last 7 days.

**Changes on the forem branch `cio-dev-id-fallback`:**
- **The fix:** `app/models/user.rb` now returns `ForemInstance.smtp_enabled? && super`. With a new regression spec in `spec/models/user_spec.rb`, which fails without the fix.
- **Existing orphans:** the data-update script that merges the email-keyed profiles into the MLH profiles is still there. Those orphans are real either way.
- **Tests:** 606 examples in the user, authentication and registrations specs. The only 2 failures are in `registrations_spec.rb` (lines 329 and 528), and they fail on main as well.

**Still open: email/password signups, about 18% or ~300 a day.** They genuinely need a confirmation email before the Core link exists, so they'd still create email-keyed orphans. Two ways to handle them:
1. **Hold their confirmation email until the MLH link lands, then send it by the Core id (recommended).** That's Core's rule: send only to a real id. The cost is roughly 30 seconds more latency on that one email, and we'd need a timeout fallback.
2. **Keep sending by email, and have Core merge `{id: email}` into the person when it links.** No latency, but it keeps email-as-id profiles around briefly.

Which do you want for email/password signups?
how long would it be in between them requesting the email and core updating the id and then it sending?

For email/password signups the MLH link usually lands within a few seconds, but there's a slow tail. Last 7 days, 1,905 signups:

| Signup → MLH link on DEV | Signups | Cumulative |
|---|---|---|
| < 5s | 1,457 | 76% |
| 5–15s | 231 | 89% |
| 15–30s | 70 | 92% |
| 30–60s | 58 | 95% |
| 1–2 min | 34 | 97% |
| 2–10 min | 29 | 99% |
| > 10 min | 26 | 1.4% |

With a "hold until linked" retry that checks every 5 seconds, the confirmation email would take about 5–10s for most people, under a minute for 95%, and several minutes for the last few percent. The last 1–2% would need a timeout that falls back to sending by email; that small group would still produce orphans.

Core may not have created the person in CIO yet when DEV sends by the Core id. That's fine: the send creates the person with the right id, and Core's identify then fills in that same person.

**Recommendation:** hold for up to about 2 minutes, then fall back to sending by email. That covers 97% with no orphan and adds about 5s for a typical signup. content.text:
You can get zero email-keyed orphans by never sending through CIO until the account is linked. DEV still has SMTP (SendGrid): `ForemInstance.smtp_enabled?` is true in prod, since that's what sends confirmations today. That gives a fallback that never touches CIO.

1. **Hold, then fall back to SMTP (recommended).** Retry the send via CIO every ~5s until the MLH link exists, which covers about 97% within 2 minutes. After 2 minutes, send through SendGrid instead. Most confirmations take about 5–10s, and none create a CIO person.
2. **Send all pre-link mail via SMTP.** For a DEV user with no MLH link, skip CIO entirely. It's the smallest change and adds no delay, but pre-link email (mostly email/password confirmations, ~300 a day) stays off CIO. That means no CIO template or tracking for it.
3. **Hold with no fallback.** It always goes through CIO, but the ~1.4% that take over 10 minutes to link, or never link, wait that long for their confirmation email or never get it. I don't recommend it.

Options 1 and 2 both depend on SendGrid staying configured. If the CIO cutover plan is to remove SendGrid, then option 3 is the only one that creates no orphans, and we'd need to fix whatever makes that last 1.4% slow.

Which one? The existing-orphan cleanup script and the OAuth confirmation fix stay either way.
no smtp allowed either - only customerio

input.new_string:
# People in Customer.io are keyed by MLH Core user id (DEV profiles were
  # stitched via the dev:<id> anonymous id). Users are never keyed by email --
  # hold_until_linked waits for the id instead -- so email only identifies
  # recipients who are not users at all.
  def customerio_identifiers
    customerio_recipient ? { id: customerio_mlh_uid } : { email: mail.to.first }
  end

  def customerio_mlh_uid
    return @customerio_mlh_uid if defined?(@customerio_mlh_uid)

    @customerio_mlh_uid = customerio_recipient&.identities&.where(provider: "mlh")&.pick(:uid)
  end

  # A new user's mlh identity lands seconds after signup (76% within 5s, 97%
  # within 2m), but signup-time mail (confirmation, magic link) goes out first.
  # Keying that send by email would mint a Customer.io person Core's id-keyed
  # person never merges with, so skip it and re-run the same mailer call once
  # the link has had time to land. Users who never link are ones Core rejected
  # (disposable domains, no email); after ~1h they are dropped, not mailed.
  def hold_until_linked
    message.perform_deliveries = false
    attempt = params.to_h.fetch(:customerio_link_hold, 0) + 1
    if attempt > CUSTOMERIO_LINK_HOLD_ATTEMPTS
      Rails.logger.warn("[Deliverable] dropped #{self.class.name}##{action_name} for unlinked user #{customerio_recipient.id}")
      return
    end

    self.class.with(params.to_h.merge(customerio_link_hold: attempt))
      .public_send(action_name, *@customerio_action_args)
      .deliver_later(wait: [2**attempt, 300].min.seconds)
  end

CUSTOMERIO_BROADCAST_PASSTHROUGH_FLAG = :customerio_broadcast_passthrough

  # Backoff is 2^n seconds capped at 5 minutes, so 20 holds span ~1 hour.
  CUSTOMERIO_LINK_HOLD_ATTEMPTS = 20

  included do
    before_action :set_perform_deliveries
    after_action  :set_delivery_options
  end

  # Kept so hold_until_linked can replay the exact mailer call.
  def process(method_name, *args)
    @customerio_action_args = args
    super
  end

DEV now never keys a user by email in Customer.io. Mail to a user without an MLH link waits for the link and then goes out keyed by their Core id. It's all on forem branch `cio-dev-id-fallback`, uncommitted; Core needs no changes.

**What changed:**
1. **Hold until linked** (`app/mailers/concerns/deliverable.rb`): if a message goes through Customer.io and the recipient is a DEV user with no MLH link, it isn't sent. The same mailer call is queued again after 2s, 4s, 8s and so on, capped at 5 minutes between tries. Once the link exists it sends with `{ id: <Core uid> }`.
2. **Drop after ~1 hour:** a user still unlinked after 20 tries is logged and not emailed. In the last 7 days those were almost all disposable-domain spam or accounts with no email, which Core rejects.
3. **OAuth confirmation fix** (`app/models/user.rb`): `confirmation_required?` is now `ForemInstance.smtp_enabled? && super`. Already-confirmed OAuth signups (82% of signups) no longer get a "confirm your account" email, which was what created both orphans you found.
4. **Cleanup of existing orphans:** the data-update script merges the existing email-keyed profiles into the MLH profiles. It's scoped to users created since 2026-07-16, about 105k candidates, in batches of 1,000.

**What users will notice:**
- Email/password confirmations and magic-link sign-in emails for brand-new users arrive a few seconds late: about 5–10s typically, under a minute for 95%.
- Magic-link signup sends its email synchronously today, so it now returns before the email is actually sent.
- Recipients who aren't DEV users at all, like exports or contact emails sent to a bare address, are still keyed by email. There's no Core id to wait for in those cases.

**Tests:** 717 examples across the mailer, user, delivery-method, magic-link and cleanup-script specs. The 6 that fail also fail on main:
- `application_mailer_spec` :8 and :150
- `devise_mailer_spec` port edge case (:246 on main, :271 on this branch)
- `magic_links_spec` :62, :83 and :98

Specs where a mailer sends through Customer.io now link the recipient first with a new `link_mlh_identity` helper. There are also new regression specs for the hold, the drop, the Devise replay and the confirmation fix.

## What type of PR is this? (check all applicable)

- [ ] Refactor

## Description

New DEV signups were getting two Customer.io profiles that never merge. DEV sends signup-time mail (confirmation instructions) within a second of signup, before Core has pushed back the `mlh` identity (~32s later on average). With no Core uid yet, `Deliverable#customerio_identifiers` fell back to `{ email: }`. Customer.io stored that address as the person's **id**, so Core's later identify with `id = <Core uuid>` created a second person. The `dev:<id>` anonymous-id stitch doesn't help here: the App and Track entity APIs only accept `id`/`email`/`cio_id`.

This follows Core's rule: only mail a person by their real id.

- **Hold until linked** (`Deliverable#hold_until_linked`): Customer.io-routed mail to a user with no `mlh` identity is skipped and the same mailer call is re-enqueued with backoff (2^n s, capped at 5 min, 20 attempts ≈ 1h). Once linked, it sends keyed by the Core uid. There is no email or SMTP fallback. Users still unlinked after ~1h are logged and dropped; in the last 7 days these were almost all disposable-domain spam or accounts with no email, which Core rejects. Recipients who are not users at all are still keyed by email.

content.text:
Here's what that bug is and the evidence for it.

**The bug.** Devise's `Confirmable` sends the "confirm your account" email from an `after_commit … on: :create` callback. It only fires when `send_confirmation_notification?` is true:

```ruby
confirmation_required? && !@skip_confirmation_notification && email.present?
```

Devise's default `confirmation_required?` is `!confirmed?`. In 2021, #13650 ("Allow sign up without email smtp config") overrode it in `User` so that instances without SMTP wouldn't require confirmation:

```ruby
def confirmation_required?
  ForemInstance.smtp_enabled?   # was: !confirmed?
end
```

That override replaced the `!confirmed?` check instead of adding to it. The OAuth signup path (`Authentication::Authenticator`) calls `user.skip_confirmation!`, which sets `confirmed_at` before the save. The override ignores that, so every OAuth signup on an instance with SMTP still gets the email. Magic-link signup doesn't hit this because it explicitly calls `skip_confirmation_notification!` (`magic_links_controller.rb:47`). The OAuth path never did.

**Evidence from the two users you reported.** Both got transactional message 50 (`dev_confirmation_instructions`) in the same second they signed up, even though `confirmed_at` was already set:
- **siyadyusuf** (GitHub): confirmed 19:03:46.249, user row 19:03:46.295. "Siyad Yusuf, confirm your DEV Community account" was delivered at 19:03:47 to the orphan `…f894d602`.
- **saumyab1** (Google): confirmed 17:02:43.054, user row 17:02:43.080. "Saumya Brahmbhatt, confirm your DEV Community account" was delivered at 17:02:43 to the orphan `…8f92d602`.

The email lands about 30 seconds before the MLH link exists, so it's keyed by email, and that creates the orphan.

**Scale.** 9,333 of 11,398 signups in the last 7 days were OAuth. By the code path, all of them get this email. It only goes through CIO (and only creates an orphan) for users in the `customerio_email_delivery` rollout; the rest go out through SendGrid, where it's pointless but harmless. CIO sent message 50 3,497 times in the last 7 days. Email/password signups alone were about 2,065 (not all on the CIO flag), so the OAuth confirmations make up a large share of those sends. I can't split the exact number from the CIO metrics.

**The fix** is `ForemInstance.smtp_enabled? && super`. It keeps the 2021 intent (no confirmation without SMTP) and restores Devise's `!confirmed?`.
- Unconfirmed email/password signups behave exactly as before.
- `active_for_authentication?` is unaffected, since confirmed users pass either way.
- Email-change reconfirmation goes through a separate Devise path (`reconfirmation_required?`), so it's untouched.

Apart from the orphans, this also stops a confusing email: if an OAuth user clicked that link, Devise would just say the account is already confirmed.

Everything else DEV sends them is unchanged: notifications, digest, sign-in and security emails. If any of those went out in the seconds before Core links the account, the new hold would delay it until the link lands and then send it keyed by the Core id. In practice an OAuth user rarely gets DEV mail in their first ~30 seconds now that the confirmation is gone.

The onboarding drip isn't affected. It's a Customer.io campaign triggered by the `user_created` CDP event, which uses the `dev:<id>` anonymous-id stitch, not DEV's mailers.

content.text:
No, Core isn't involved. DEV confirms OAuth accounts itself at signup. `Authentication::Authenticator` (`app/services/authentication/authenticator.rb:229`) calls `user.skip_confirmation!` when it creates the user, which sets `confirmed_at` straight away. It's trusting that the OAuth provider (GitHub, Google, Apple and so on) already owns the email address. That's why both users' `confirmed_at` is a few milliseconds *before* their `created_at`.

DEV doesn't check a per-provider "email verified" flag itself; the provider's OmniAuth strategy decides which email it hands over. The PR doesn't change any of that. Those users were already treated as confirmed, and the only difference is that they no longer get an email asking them to confirm again.

Core only comes into it afterwards, when the sync reads DEV's `confirmed_at` to decide whether to trust the email for identity. It doesn't set it.

class DataUpdateWorker
  include Sidekiq::Job
  sidekiq_options queue: :high_priority, retry: 5

  def perform(id = nil)
    if id
      data_update_script = DataUpdateScript.find(id)
      data_update_script.mark_as_run!
      log_status(data_update_script)
      run_script(data_update_script)
    else
      DataUpdateScript.scripts_to_run.each do |script|
        script.mark_as_run!
        log_status(script)
        run_script(script)
      end
    end
  end

  private

  def run_script(script)
    require script.file_path

    script.file_class.new.run

    script.mark_as_finished!
    log_status(script)
  rescue StandardError => e
    script.mark_as_failed!(e)
    log_status(script)

    Honeybadger.notify(e, context: { script_id: script.id })
  end

  def log_status(script)
    status = script.status
    file_name = script.file_name

namespace :data_updates do
  desc "Enqueue Sidekiq worker to handle data updates"
  task enqueue_data_update_worker: :environment do
    if Rails.env.development?
      Rake::Task["data_updates:run"].execute
    else
      # @mstruve: Due to many folks already hosting their Forems on Heroku lets
      # set a friendly default for them. Ideally we get everyone to use
      # the ENV variable below but until we can do a hard cut over with
      # a version I think this is a good compromise
      default_delay = ENV["HEROKU_SLUG_COMMIT"].present? ? 10.minutes : 0

      # Use the env variable to delay running data update scripts if your
      # deploy strategy requires it
      DataUpdateWorker.perform_in(ENV.fetch("WORKERS_DATA_UPDATE_DELAY_SECONDS") { default_delay })
    end
  end

  desc "Run data updates"
  task run: :environment do
    DataUpdateWorker.new.perform
  end

  desc "Get data update status"
  task status: :environment do
    # Disable ActiveRecord logging for this task.
    # See: https://github.com/forem/forem/pull/13653#discussion_r626278422
    ActiveRecord::Base.logger = nil
    # rubocop:disable Style/FormatStringToken
    puts format(" %-9s  %-14s  %-40s", "Status", "ID", "Description")
    puts "-" * 80
    DataUpdateScript.find_each do |dus|
      id, file_name = dus.file_name.split("_", 2)
      puts format("%+10s  %+14s  %-40s", dus.status, id, file_name.tr("_", " "))
    end
    # rubocop:enable Style/FormatStringToken
  end
end

class DataUpdateScript < ApplicationRecord
  DIRECTORY = Rails.root.join("lib/data_update_scripts").freeze
  NAMESPACE = "DataUpdateScripts".freeze
  STATUSES = { enqueued: 0, working: 1, succeeded: 2, failed: 3 }.freeze
  resourcify

  enum :status, STATUSES

  validates :file_name, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :status, presence: true

  class << self
    def scripts_to_run
      insert_new_scripts

      enqueued.order(file_name: :asc)
    end

    # true if there are more files on disk or any scripts to run, false otherwise
    def scripts_to_run?
      db_scripts = DataUpdateScript.pluck(:file_name, :status).to_h

      return true if filenames.size > db_scripts.size
      return true if db_scripts.values.any? { |s| s.to_sym == :enqueued }

      false
    end

    private

    def filenames
      Dir.glob("*.rb", base: DIRECTORY).map do |f|
        File.basename(f, ".rb")
      end
    end

    def insert_new_scripts
      now = Time.current
      scripts_params = filenames.map do |fn|
        { file_name: fn, created_at: now, updated_at: now }
      end

      DataUpdateScript.insert_all(scripts_params)
    end
  end

  def mark_as_run!
    update!(run_at: Time.current, status: :working)
  end

  def mark_as_finished!
    update!(finished_at: Time.current, status: :succeeded, error: nil)
  end

  def mark_as_failed!(err)
    update!(
      finished_at: Time.current,
      status: :failed,
      error: "#{err.class}: #{err.message}",
    )

content.text:
The cleanup script failed in production on its first query, before it sent any merges. I opened a fix: https://github.com/forem/forem/pull/23861

**Why it failed:** it ran at 00:09:21 UTC and stopped 3 seconds later with a statement timeout. The script processes users in batches ordered by `users.id`, so the first query walked about 4M older users from id 1 to find the ~107k it wanted. That's well over the 2.5s timeout.

**The fix:**
- It now looks up the first user id created since the rollout (4,031,131), using the `created_at` index, and batches forward from there. I checked the new query against the prod replica and it returns fast. The script's spec passes.
- I gave the script a new timestamp, `20260923010000`, so it runs automatically on the next deploy. The worker that runs these scripts never retries one that failed. The old `20260922120000` row will stay marked `failed`, but nothing ran under it.

**Container build log:** that failure isn't ours, and it didn't affect the Heroku deploy. The build script works out the date tag twice, once at build and once at push, and this run crossed midnight UTC between them (`tag does not exist: …:20260923`). Retrying the Buildkite step will pass. I can also make the one-line fix so the date is computed once.

Once #23861 is merged and deployed, I'll check that the script succeeded and that your two email-keyed profiles are gone from Customer.io.

They only show a `merge` action in the single-person Track v2 reference; every batch example uses `identify` or relationships. CUSTOMERIO_TRACK_API.merge_customers("id", "01a0c55a-6041-4642-1e7d-77aa73dbf708", "id", "siyadyusuf@outlook.com")
