content.text:
Datadog shows the script did exactly what it was written to do; the problem is on Customer.io's side.

**What the Datadog trace shows (`DataUpdateWorker`, trace 4217203746058845351, sidekiq_worker.1, deployed version `6f1057e`):**
- **01:02:57.098:** the start-id lookup (`ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 1`) took 2ms. The `created_at` index fix worked.
- **01:02:57 → 01:03:41:** it ran the planned loop 108 times: fetch the next 1,000 user ids (~100ms), look up their MLH uid and email (~20–60ms), then `POST track.customer.io/api/v2/batch`.
  - All 108 POSTs returned HTTP 200.
  - Most took 100–300ms; one took 4.4s at 01:03:33, and one took 1.3s at 01:03:38.
  - No errors or retries anywhere in the trace.
- **01:03:41.67:** the script was marked succeeded and the job ended cleanly after 44.6s.
- **App logs:** nothing from the script or `DataUpdateWorker` in the Heroku logs for that window. The script doesn't log anything itself.

So DEV sent all ~107k merges, and Customer.io's batch endpoint accepted every request without reporting a single per-item error. The merges still haven't been applied 20+ minutes later, even though Customer.io's own merge preview says the Siyad pair is mergeable.

Datadog doesn't record response bodies, so it can't tell us why Customer.io dropped them. That still takes the single v1 `merge_customers` call from a console. Its response comes back synchronously and shows whether this kind of merge works at all:

```ruby
CUSTOMERIO_TRACK_API.merge_customers("id", "01a0c55a-6041-4642-1e7d-77aa73dbf708", "id", "siyadyusuf@outlook.com")
```

module Emails
  # Merges the email-keyed Customer.io person minted for a user mailed before
  # their mlh identity landed into their Core-keyed person, for the users in
  # [start_id, end_id]. Enqueued by the MergeEmailKeyedCustomerioProfiles data
  # update script.
  #
  # One v1 merge per user: /api/v2/batch accepts "merge" ops with a 200 and
  # never applies them. A merge whose secondary does not exist is also a 200,
  # so users without an orphan are harmless no-ops, and merges are idempotent,
  # so a retry after a 429 just redoes the range.
  class MergeEmailKeyedCustomerioProfilesWorker
    include Sidekiq::Job

    sidekiq_options queue: :low_priority, retry: 10

    def perform(start_id, end_id)
      User.where(id: start_id..end_id)
        .where.not(email: [nil, ""])
        .joins(:identities)
        .where(identities: { provider: "mlh" })
        .where("identities.created_at > users.created_at")
        .pluck("identities.uid", "users.email")
        .each { |uid, email| CUSTOMERIO_TRACK_API.merge_customers("id", uid, "id", email) }
    end
  end
end

module DataUpdateScripts
  # Before Deliverable held mail for users without an mlh identity, mail sent
  # to a new user before that link landed was keyed by email. Customer.io
  # stored that address as the person's id, leaving an orphan profile beside
  # the one keyed by the MLH uid that nothing ever merges. Merge each orphan
  # into its linked person.
  #
  # Scoped to users created since Customer.io delivery shipped (2026-07-16) --
  # the only accounts that could have been mailed unlinked. The merges run as
  # one worker per id range, staggered so ~107k Track API calls stay well under
  # the rate limit and a deploy restart only interrupts a single range.
  class MergeEmailKeyedCustomerioProfiles
    ROLLOUT_DATE = Time.zone.parse("2026-07-16")
    RANGE_SIZE = 1_000
    STAGGER = 1.minute

    def run
      return unless ForemInstance.customerio_track_enabled?

      # Not minimum(:id) -- Postgres plans that as a filtered primary key walk
      # over every older user; ordering by created_at reads its index instead.
      start_id = User.where(created_at: ROLLOUT_DATE..).order(:created_at).pick(:id)
      return unless start_id

      (start_id..User.maximum(:id)).step(RANGE_SIZE).each_with_index do |range_start, i|
        Emails::MergeEmailKeyedCustomerioProfilesWorker
          .perform_in(i * STAGGER, range_start, range_start + RANGE_SIZE - 1)
      end
    end
  end
end

    described_class.new.perform(pre_linked.id, pre_linked.id)

    expect(track_client).not_to have_received(:merge_customers)
  end
